newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wholesaler stocks at low level in November.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wholesaler stocks at low level in November.

text.p: A jump in sales in November left wholesalers with their lowest levels of inventories in more than six years, the Commerce Department said Thursday.
Wholesalers had only 1.26 months' worth of goods on hand in November, the lowest level since March 1990.
The so-called inventories-to-sales ratio, which measures how long it would take to sell existing inventories at the current prices, was down from 1.27 months' worth in October.
Actual inventories edged up a scant 0.1 percent in November to a seasonally adjusted $258.02 billion after growing by 0.3 percent in October, the department said.

Increases were recorded mainly in stocks of long-lasting durable goods, which rose 0.3 percent to $163.58 billion. Gains were strongest in inventories of metals, electrical supplies and hardware, the department said.
Inventories of nondurable goods, ranging from paper to food and chemicals, fell 0.2 percent to $94.43 billion in November.
Petroleum stocks, which typically grow in advance of the winter heating season, rose by 1.1 percent in November after a sharp 6.5 percent rise in October.

Wholesale sales gains far outpaced the scant growth in inventories, jumping by 0.9 percent in November to $204.58 billion after a 0.7 percent rise in October. It was their biggest increase since July.
Sales growth was strongest in durable goods, which rose 1.5 percent in November. Sales were paced by gains in furniture, professional equipment, metal and machinery sales.
But sales of automotive products, which represent factory deliveries to dealers, fell 0.3 percent to $16.86 billion in November after a 0.7 percent drop in October.
Sales of non-durable goods rose only 0.3 percent.
